Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play reversi/othello, see Tips_reversi The game starts with two black and two white pieces in the board's centre. Black and white take turns to add pieces to the board. On your turn you must place a piece such that there is an unbroken line of opponent pieces between your added piece and another piece of your colour (horizontal, vertical or diagonal). When you place such a piece, flip the line of opposing pieces to your colour. If you cannot place a piece, you must pass. The game ends when the board is full, or when neither player can make a valid move. The game is won by player with the most pieces of their colour visible. [Rating: 2/10] I'm rubbish at this game.  Very frustrating when loads of your pieces get turned over.  My dad made me a set with buttons and a homemade board.

[Rating: 2/10] Well, this is a real game, but when you can write an ai which beats yourself there's no mind in playing it any more.

[Rating: 2/10] I played this online a lot in the past. My first favorite board game. Until I realized it was more depriving your opponent of moves than a race for the corners and edges. Then I liked the game less.  1+1

[Rating: 2/10] ----------  Boring, bland, dry, and old.  This, to me, is the epitome of a "bored game."  Sure, there's plenty of strategy to be had here, but why waste your time getting good at such a terrible game when you could be playing something so much more fun? There is nothing in my being that would find enjoyment out of flipping disks.... I much rather prefer pushing cubes =)  ----------

[Rating: 2/10] This is a good looking abstract game, but I always feel that it lacks something.  There is a strong dependance on turn order, and experience makes a huge difference in play.  While it is quick to play, I find I just don't care for it anymore.  I see it as basically a kids game.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't think I ever liked this. I understood the importance of edges and corners, but my older brother got them anyway. No desire to catch up on the theory of how to do that.  Thrifted on 21/11 2015 (as Traveller Series Reversi), 29/6 2019, 5/2 2020, 5/8 2021, 6/10 2022, 11/2 2026, 30/4 2026 and 27/5 2026.

[Rating: 2/10] 1 / 5 - Bad.  My poor rating for this is influenced by the fact that I totally suck at it, even more than I usually do at abstracts. And I don't like abstracts in the first place. It doesn't help that it's easy to completely ruin a game by not spotting all the possible "flips" after a given move.
